output:
@ReneeK_Meyerland Renee, I am truly sorry your toe became red, swollen and painful, and that you ended up at urgent care on antibiotics. I really mean that. You have been my customer for two years, and I do not want this to become a public fight. I am also sorry if you felt that I shrugged or did not care when you came back. That was never my intention.

I would like to explain what happened and how we work, calmly.

Your deluxe pedicure on Saturday, October 24 was $45, and Vy was your technician. During the pedicure, Vy remembers that you asked her more than once to cut the cuticle further because you wanted it very clean. She told you she should not cut too much, and you told her it was fine because you always had it done that way. I am sharing this so the whole conversation during the service is understood, not to blame you or say your pain was not real.

When you returned on November 2 and showed me your toe, I offered you the full $45 refund and also offered to pay your urgent-care copay if you brought me the receipt. You then asked for $300 cash and free pedicures for one year. That specific request is what I said no to. I did not refuse the refund or the copay. Both offers are still open to you.

For the people reading this, every reusable tool at Lotus Garden is sterilized in my autoclave and kept in a sealed pouch. We open the pouch in front of the customer. Files and buffers are new for each person, and the customer may take them home. We use a new plastic liner in the pedicure tub every time. We passed our state inspection in August 2026 with no violations, and the inspection paperwork is posted on our wall. Anyone is welcome to look at it.

Renee, you also said Vy barely speaks English. Vy is my niece, she was born here in Houston, and she has been a licensed nail technician for three years. She speaks English; she is simply shy. I understand that a shy person can sometimes be harder to talk with, but her shyness is not a lack of English or training. Reading these comments has been very hard on her. She cried in our back room and told me she wanted to quit doing nails. I mention that only to ask people to remember there is a real person behind these comments.

I opened Lotus Garden in 2007 after working for my aunt. In 19 years in Houston, this is the first infection complaint brought to me. What hurts me most is seeing this become a discussion about how all salons like mine are dirty, as though we are all the same. I cannot speak for other businesses, but I can stand behind our sanitation practices and our inspection record. Renee, you mentioned filing with the state, and of course I will cooperate fully with anything they request.

@MarisolB, thank you for sharing your experience kindly and for suggesting that Renee and I talk again. I appreciate that very much.

Renee, my offer remains the same: I will give you the full $45 refund and pay your urgent-care copay when you provide the receipt. If you are willing, please call me at the salon phone number or come in and ask to speak with me privately. I will make time for you. I would much rather listen and talk with you directly than continue answering each other online.
